text:
anya: Quick sync — thinking through a pattern: regional control plane remains centralized, but we push a lightweight relay/edge agent into customer VPCs to handle egress, NAT preservation, and private endpoints. Goal is avoid per-customer peering while keeping control plane isolation for Private customers.
ben: Sounds promising. Main concerns: IP preservation for customers wanting stable egress IPs, and auditability (we need flow logs tied to customer tenant ids).
anya: Exactly. Relay would maintain tenant-specific SNAT mappings so we can present stable egress IPs without full VPC peering. Relay would be managed by us but run in customer subnets (sidecar/daemonset in k8s on their infra or our lightweight VM image for on-prem).
infra-bot: Note: previous spike showed hairpinning issues with shared NAT + proxying on AWS Transit Gateway. See logs: `tgw-hairpin-2024-06`.
kevin: For AWS customers: if relay does SNAT, we must avoid overlapping customer CIDRs. We'll also need an option to allocate Elastic IPs per-tenant vs shared pool. Allocating per-tenant EIP is expensive at scale.
sara: What about using a small per-customer proxy pool in our region that does outbound egress via a shared set of public IPs but preserves tenant identity in headers and logs? Then for customers that absolutely require a static IP we offer dedicated EIP option.
ben: That feels like the cost-tier model we already offer for Dedicated. For Private, compliance often mandates traffic stay on customer-owned IPs or within VPC. So relay-in-VPC with SNAT -> tenant EIP is required for some.
anya: Right — propose three modes:
1) In-VPC relay with tenant-controlled EIP (full isolation, higher infra ops cost)
2) In-VPC relay with shared EIP pool and tenant SNAT mapping (cheaper, still in-customer VPC)
3) Regional relay (our infra) with tenant headers for Private customers who accept egress via our IPs
kevin: Edge case: on-prem air-gapped customers — relay must be able to fallback to direct control-plane-less polling for config updates. That drives design of the handshake protocol.
anya: Agree. Handshake: relay uses mTLS to the control plane; support a fallback mode where relay pulls signed config blobs from an S3-like artifact store inside customer network if control plane absent. That preserves audit trail via signed manifests.
infra-bot: Reminder: KMS integration required for signed manifests. Existing KMS connectors: AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS.
sara: Operationally: we need a clear failure mode for control plane loss — do we fail open (continue serving cached policies) or fail closed (drop requests)? For some regulated customers fail-closed is required.
ben: We should make fail-mode per-tenant config. Default: fail-open for availability, with fail-closed opt-in.
anya: Scaling note: relays should be stateless besides SNAT table which can be rebuilt from control plane on restart. Prefer ephemeral instances behind ASG/VM scale sets; persistent mapping stored in control plane database so new relays can rehydrate.
kevin: One tricky part: cross-AZ egress latency if we put relay in customer's VPC but control plane in a different region. Keep relay-local dataplane, minimize control plane chattiness. Use long-lived KV cache + delta updates.
sara: Also add telemetry: per-request tenant id, model id, route id, and a small sampling of tokens for quality/debug (encrypted at rest). Make sure logs live in customer account for Private with option to forward to our observability for Hosted customers.
anya: Next steps: draft RFC with API for relay handshake, config manifest schema, and three-mode pricing/ops playbook. I'll sketch a config example:

```
relay-config: {
  tenant_id: "ten-123",
  mode: "in-vpc-shared-eip",
  snat_mappings: ["10.0.0.0/24 => 54.12.34.56"],
  fail_mode: "fail-open",
  kms_key: "arn:aws:kms:...",
}
```

ben: Looks good. Add a field for allowed_control_plane_endpoints to support regional pinning.
anya: Will do. Assigning RFC draft to me, pinging @kevin for operational checklist and @sara for security/compliance notes. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll add migration steps for customers moving from peering to relay model and a validation plan (connectivity, egress ip validation, perf tests).
sara: I'll write the compliance matrix: fail-closed requirements, audit log retention, and KMS/Audit key management guidance.
infra-bot: RFC created: rfc/2024-ctrlplane-relay-pattern-draft (internal link)
anya: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the short decision log for the initial design. If anyone has objections to three-mode approach speak now, otherwise I'll start RFC PR.
ben: No objections from me.
kevin: SGTM.
sara: SGTM.
anya: PR incoming tomorrow.
